clue.text: Hindu convert to Islam changed by hadj, OK?

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A Hindu's conversion to Islam is sealed by making the pilgrimage to Mecca, and someone asks whether that is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The hadj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, which keeps the surface on topic while lending the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A khodja (khoja) is a member of an Ismaili Muslim community descended from Hindu converts.

clue.text: Spinning like Gandhi? You could end up with this linge

definitions.text: Spinning like Gandhi? You could end up with this linge

indicators.note: spinning sets things turning round, so the letters of the following words are churned into a new order
what you end up with is what is left over once the stated extra letters have been taken out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written: ten letters to be stirred
taken as written; linge is French for linen, and these letters are the part left over

explanation.surface: Gandhi famously spun cloth by hand; spin as he did and you would end up with linen of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the letters of LIKE GANDHI rearrange as the answer plus LINGE, so removing LINGE leaves KHADI. The whole clue also describes the cloth Gandhi spun.
explanation.definitionFit: Khadi is hand-spun, hand-woven Indian cotton cloth, promoted by Gandhi as a symbol of self-reliance.

clue.text: Feeding wholly on organisms (three eggs scrambled with zilch)

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are beaten together, so the letters here are mixed into a new order

parts.note: an egg is O for its shape, so three of them give three Os
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diet note: living wholly on whole organisms, here three scrambled eggs and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' fits the eggs so naturally that it hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Holozoic organisms, like most animals, take in solid organic matter by ingesting other organisms.

clue.text: Automatic recording device, a lot randomized within obelus (10, two words)

indicators.note: within tells us the jumbled letters go inside the following word
randomized means put in no fixed order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words rearranged
an obelus is the dagger sign used in printing

explanation.surface: A technical description of a recording gadget whose output has been jumbled inside a printed mark.
explanation.walkthrough: An obelus is the printer's dagger sign (†), used to mark footnotes or obsolete words; the mixed-up letters are slipped in after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A data logger is an electronic instrument that automatically records measurements over time.

clue.text: Japanese granny displays such spiritual knowledge

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for Japanese
nana is a familiar word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A wise Japanese grandmother shows a kind of spiritual insight.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu philosophy jnana is knowledge, especially the spiritual knowledge that leads to liberation.

clue.text: E.g. croup a nag loosely holds on the spot

definitions.note: croup is an example of the old general sense of the word

indicators.note: loosely suggests something not held in its set arrangement, so these letters are reordered
holds means the jumbled letters wrap round the next element

parts.note: the two words rearranged
in can mean present, on the spot

explanation.surface: A loosely held horse pictured beside a cough remedy note, croup being the example given.
explanation.walkthrough: Croup tempts as the horse's rump, fitting the nag, but it is the childhood throat illness given as an example of the answer's old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina once meant any inflammatory throat complaint, such as quinsy or croup, before narrowing to the heart condition.

clue.text: Fixed point in depression recalled e.g. Electra

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the combined letters are read from the end
in places one word inside the other before anything else is done

parts.note: a dip is a hollow or depression
a pole is a fixed point, such as either end of the earth's axis

explanation.surface: A fixed point in a dip is remembered, with the doomed heroine Electra offered as an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' applies to the whole combination once the fixed point is inside the depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pelopid is a descendant of Pelops, and Electra, daughter of Agamemnon, belongs to that cursed line.

clue.text: Greek letter in moral stories illustrating oversight

indicators.note: in tells us the letter's name is set inside the following word

parts.note: parables are short tales told to teach a moral
psi is the 23rd letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter turns up in a book of moral tales and shows someone has slipped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter is not set in the middle but just before the final S of the stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Parablepsis is a scribe's error of eye-skip, a copying slip or oversight in manuscripts.

clue.text: A cerebral department taken up Congo river known for disease

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a lobe is a division of the brain

explanation.surface: A brain department is taken up with studying a Congo river famous for an outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebola is a river in the Democratic Republic of Congo that gave its name to the haemorrhagic fever first found nearby.

clue.text: Glow no longer seen from within element (

indicators.note: from within says the letters come out of the inside of the next word

parts.note: the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: A glow has vanished from inside some element, as if a lamp has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Leme is an obsolete word for a gleam or glow, so it fits a light that is no longer in use.

clue.text: Skirt worn for ceremonies more and more in Rome

parts.note: più is Italian for more
the same Italian word again, Rome pointing to the language

explanation.surface: A ceremonial skirt is worn more and more often in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' tells us to use Italian, and the doubled word reflects 'more and more'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piupiu is a Maori flax skirt worn for haka and ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Axis maybe encompassing last in Soviet block?

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the axis is an Indian spotted deer, 'maybe' marking it as an example

indicators.note: last in points at the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Reads like history: the wartime Axis surrounding the Soviet bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: Axis looks like the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, but it is the spotted deer of India.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or prevent, as when an obstacle blocks someone from acting.

clue.text: Pair of animals among Noah's reproduced — praise be!

indicators.note: reproduced suggests copying in new form, so these letters are reshaped
among puts the first piece inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: the name rearranged

indicators.note: a pair of a word takes just its opening two letters

parts.note: the first two letters

explanation.surface: The animals that went into Noah's ark two by two have bred, and someone gives thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduced' fits the animals breeding, but it signals a rearrangement of NOAHS, with AN set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of praise or adoration to God, equivalent to an exclamation of 'praise be'.

clue.text: Dirty old Muslim chief protected by British Empire initially

definitions.note: a verb here: to make dirty

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed within it
initially points to the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
an emir is a Muslim ruler or commander

explanation.surface: A grubby old Muslim leader kept safe under the British Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' looks like an adjective for the old chief but is the verb. EMIR goes between the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemire is to soil with mud, so it means to make dirty.

clue.text: Slaver ante meal's specially prepared recipe

indicators.note: something specially prepared is made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A slave trader's pre-dinner dish, made by special recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaver' could mean drool, fitting the meal, but here it is a slave trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A manstealer is one who kidnaps people to sell them, a slave trader.

clue.text: Put down national airline (forget the rest)?

indicators.note: forget the rest tells us to drop the closing part of the name

parts.note: Alitalia was Italy's national airline

explanation.surface: Someone disparages the Italian national carrier and wants to forget the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests disparage, but here it means landed. The dropped ending, alia, is Latin for 'others', a neat fit for 'the rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past form of alight, used of an aircraft or bird that has landed or touched down.

clue.text: Old love affair involving gypsy and one of the family

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany man
an aunt is a family member

explanation.surface: A past romance that drew in a traveller and one of the relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Old here marks the answer as archaic, not the affair as long past.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaunt is an archaic form of romance, a tale of love and chivalry.

clue.text: Buck briefly filled with obsessive desire concerning estate?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its end
filled with means the next piece goes inside the shortened word

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, cut short
a mania is an obsessive craving

explanation.surface: A male deer gripped by obsessive desire, apparently to do with land.
explanation.walkthrough: Buck is US slang for a dollar, not a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Domanial is the adjective of domain, relating to an estate or landed property.

clue.text: Plant collections providing wherewithal for Alpert song?

parts.note: Herb Alpert is the American trumpeter; his first name completes him
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Collections of plants supply the means for a song by Herb Alpert.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb Alpert led the Tijuana Brass; 'wherewithal for Alpert' is the name that goes before his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaria are collections of dried and pressed plant specimens kept for study.

clue.text: Liveliness displayed by tailless antelope

indicators.note: tailless means without a tail, so the word's last letter goes

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope that has lost its tail still shows plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and vigour, a synonym for liveliness.

clue.text: Twiggy maybe showing full range inside underwear department?

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in osier basketwork

indicators.note: the full range inside means all the interior letters and nothing at the edges

parts.note: hosiery is the store department selling socks and underwear

explanation.surface: Twiggy, the 1960s model, perhaps displaying a full range of lingerie in a store's underwear section.
explanation.walkthrough: Twiggy suggests the model, but here it means made of twigs. Dropping the first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are used in basketry, so osier work is twiggy.

clue.text: Line on skull not available in true colours after operation (13, two words)

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the following phrase before the jumble
an operation works on something and changes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
NA is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A surgeon notices a skull line that the true colours did not show after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The coronal suture is the seam in the skull joining the frontal bone to the two parietal bones.

clue.text: King with moral justice almost avenged in Shakespeare

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
equity is fairness, justice based on moral principle

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king, morally just, is almost avenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Shakespeare' marks the answer as his usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses requit as a past form of requite, meaning repaid or avenged.

clue.text: Earthenware containers arranged as nest

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pots of earthenware set out so they stack inside one another like a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stean (steen) is a dialect word for a clay or stone jar or pitcher.

clue.text: Class no longer part of college, I see, backward

indicators.note: backward means the concealed letters are read from right to left
part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of college, I and the start of see

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a class is no longer part of the college, and seems to have fallen behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete sense: the answer once meant rank or class.
explanation.definitionFit: Siege is an obsolete word for a seat, and so for rank or class, as in a seat of standing.

clue.text: Metalworker's tool, depression on end of blade

parts.note: a swag is a hollow or depression in the ground

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A metalworker's tool with a dent near the end of its blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A swage is a tool or die used by smiths for shaping metal by hammering or pressing.

clue.text: Rummage for practical purpose

parts.note: a practical purpose is one 'to use'; the infinitive marker comes first
use is a purpose or function

explanation.surface: Someone digs about for something of practical value.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'for practical purpose' is read as 'for use', i.e. to be used, with 'for' only joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Touse is an old and dialect word meaning to pull about or tousle, to rummage roughly.

clue.text: Component of kina, or china possibly? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the next piece goes inside the word just found

parts.note: China is a kind of tea, 'possibly' marking an example
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Asks whether a part of a kina is china, perhaps with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The kina is the currency of Papua New Guinea; 'china' suggests porcelain but means a type of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The toea is the coin worth one hundredth of a Papua New Guinea kina, so it is a component of it.

clue.text: Ordinary degree lecture?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary
a rate is a degree or level, as in at a fast rate

explanation.surface: Asks whether an ordinary university degree might be called a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes a university pass degree and its lectures; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, which is what giving a lecture involves.

clue.text: A little light Scotch providing portion of tasty medicine

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters are drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of tasty and the start of medicine

explanation.surface: A splash of Scotch whisky offered as a palatable medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests whisky, but it marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a styme is a glimmer or faint gleam, a tiny amount of light.

clue.text: Duck occupying most of its frequent location, an Indian tree

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: A duck takes over most of its usual pond, near an Indian tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, so it gives O; it then sits inside POND shorn of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poon is an East Indian tree whose straight timber was used for masts and spars.

clue.text: Hot in PE, aorta throbbing — one collapses readily (8, two words)

indicators.note: in places the single letter among the letters that follow
throbbing means pulsing and agitated, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Overheated in a gym lesson, a pupil's main artery pounding, someone is ready to keel over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One collapses readily' seems to continue the fainting story but describes a folding hat. PE is physical education, the school gym lesson.

clue.text: Let down in France that involved sou after small advance

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the coin's letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is a short form of advance
que is French for that
the old French coin, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is disappointed in France by a mere sou given after a small advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' tempts as disappointed; here it is taken as watered down. Some think 'set down' (deposited by water) was intended.

clue.text: Parrot in captivity rolled over

explanation.definitionFit: A lory is a brightly coloured Australasian parrot, a kind of lorikeet.

clue.text: Grand American goes round Rio, crazy for local timpani?

the city name rearranged

clue.text: I'll be kept in during study period — it's temporary

indicators.note: to be kept in means to stay inside, so the letter goes within the phrase that follows

the pronoun I, with the contraction read as 'I will'

explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside IN TERM, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes an arrangement that holds only until something permanent replaces it, i.e. provisional.

clue.text: Film covers e.g. XXXX can's opening

parts.note: each X is the letter ex, so four make a plural, exes
a tin is a can

explanation.walkthrough: XXXX is a brand of Australian beer, but here it is just a string of the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extines are the tough outer coats or membranes of pollen grains and spores, so thin film coverings.

clue.text: Articles with 'teeth' almost stop backing English

backing means moving backwards, so the shortened word is read in reverse

parts.note: to arrest is to stop, cut short

explanation.definitionFit: Serrae are saw-like structures or organs in zoology, things edged with tooth-like projections.
